steps.title: From memory
body: A **cold rebuild** is one of your own Sidekick pieces, written again from a blank editor: no starter, no hints, no solution to reveal. Pulling it out of your own head is what makes it stay there.
The full `sk find` compiler is long, so today you rebuild its core, a **short form**:
- with `>`, `<` or `=` and a whole number,
If you can build this tree by hand from memory, the rest of the full version is more of the same.

steps.prompt: Why does `CompileFilter` return an `Expression<Func<TaskItem, bool>>` instead of a `Func<TaskItem, bool>`?
options: A tree can be inspected, printed or translated (to SQL by EF Core), and still compiled when needed
steps.explain: A delegate is compiled code you can only call. A tree is data: `sk find` prints it, an `IQueryable` provider translates it, and `Compile()` still turns it into a delegate.

steps.title: Rebuild the filter compiler (short form)
prompt: From memory. Your `TaskItem` is given, with `System.Linq.Expressions` and `System.Text.RegularExpressions` in place.
- `query` is one or more conditions joined by `and` (any case, spaces around it).
- A condition is `minutes` or `estimate` (any case), then `>`, `<` or `=`, then a whole number; spaces around the operator are allowed. `minutes` is `LoggedMinutes`, `estimate` is `EstimateMinutes`.
- Join the conditions with `Expression.AndAlso`. Anything else (another field, another operator, not a number, an empty query, `or`) throws `FormatException`.
solution: if (!m.Success) throw new FormatException($"I can't read \"{part}\"");
body = body is null ? test : Expression.AndAlso(body, test);
